rationale: Both candidates independently nail the three substantive live concerns (missing @RuixiangMa on diffusion/models, the misleading 'preserves prior ownership' LoRA comment, and the offloader.md description-vs-code Isotr0py mismatch), and both catch several of the same secondary issues (plugins/model_extras owner mismatch, stale stage_configs/ path, over-broad distributed/ rule) — strong cross-validation that these are real. X reads as a much more usable review: clear verdict, prioritized blocking/correctness/process sections, and crisp 'Change:' instructions, but leans on unverifiable precision claims (exact multi-hundred file blast-radius counts, specific commit hashes) that inflate apparent rigor without shown evidence. Y is more transparent and better grounded (quotes exact diff/grep evidence per claim) and adds one genuinely valuable extra catch (a test file referencing the now-dead stage_configs path), but its output is denser, harder to scan, and cuts off mid-sentence in the additional-observations section. Neither includes a LATENT GAP CHECK section.
